html.body: Date: 2025-03-07 REMARKSThe Office Action has been received and carefully noted. The above amendments to the claims, and the following remarks, are submitted as a full and complete response thereto.Claims 6-9, 11, and 13-18 have been amended. Support for the claim amendments can be found at least in paragraphs [0020], [0021], [0027], [0043], [0044], [0052], [0054], [0067], [0068], [0124], [0130], [0151], and [0152] of the subject application. Claims 1-5, 10, 12, 19, and 20 have been cancelled without prejudice to or disclaimer of the subject matter recited therein. Claims 21- 29 have been added. Support for the new claims can be found in at least in paragraphs [0020], [0021], [0027], [0043], [0044], [0052], [0054], [0067], [0068], [0124], [0130], [0151], and [0152].No new matter is added. Claims 6-9, 11, 13-18, and 21-29 are currently pending in the application, of which claims 6, 28, and 29 are independent claims. Further examination and reconsideration of the application is respectfully requested.Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 / 103 The Office Action presented the following rejections.* Claims 1-16, 18, and 19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102(a)(1) and (2) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 3,670,999 ("Leger").* Claims 15 and 17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Leger in view of U.S. Patent No. 3,781,055 ("Keich").* Claim 20 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Leger in view of EP Patent No. 3,293,116 ("Jones").In the field of aerial delivery, it is typical that a cargo is extracted from a cargo bay of an aircraft under the action of an extraction parachute. After exiting the aircraft, the extraction parachute is released from the cargo and the main parachute is deployed to bring the cargo to the ground. The main parachute is typically deployed by the extraction parachute pulling on a main parachute deployment line after the extraction parachute has been released from the cargo.The aerial delivery system according to some embodiments includes two key assemblies - (1) an extraction assembly 100 and (2) extraction parachute release assembly 200. See Figures 1, 2 and 16 (reproduced below).--- Extraction asserbiv Extraction parachute release assembly The extraction assembly includes a coupling arrangement 120. In some embodiments, the coupling arrangement includes a first coupling portion 121 to which the extraction line 18 of the extraction parachute 16 is attached, and a second coupling portion 122 to which the main parachute deployment line 15 is attached. In a first stage, at a first predetermined moment during extraction of the platform 11, corresponding to a first predetermined position of the platform 11 relative to the aircraft 1, the coupling device 130 switches the coupling arrangement 120 from the open configuration to the closed configuration. In a second stage, at a second predetermined moment during extraction of the platform 11, corresponding to a second predetermined position of the platform 11 relative to the aircraft 1, the extraction parachute release assembly 200 causes the extraction parachute release device 140 to uncouple the extraction parachute 16. The above stages occur when the drop arms 160, 231, positioned at different points on the platform 11, rotate upon exiting the aircraft 1. See paragraphs [0225] and [0228].Leger Leger discusses a force transfer mechanism 23 for connecting an extraction parachute line 18 to a main parachute deployment line 21. See Fig. 1.49 X16 /0 23 The force transfer mechanism 23 comprises a first link 49 for connection to the extraction parachute line 18, and a second link 50 for connection to the main parachute deployment line 21.During extraction, the first link 49 is initially retained by rollers 84, 85 which are positioned at the end of pivotally mounted link retainer 78. See Fig. 9. The second link 50 is nested within the first link 49, and initially the first and second links 49, 50 are not connected to each other. See Fig. 3.Theffr m m 2i t . - I t I I-i The force transfer mechanism 23 has a crankshaft 37 which is rotated when a crank arm 38 passes a fixture 28 on the aircraft floor 16 during extraction. Rotation of the camshaft 37 causes a locking pin 51 to move and connect the first link 49 and the second link 50. See Fig. 4. Rotation of the crankshaft 37 also causes the rollers 84, 85 to move and release first link 49. With the first and second links 49, 50 connected and with the first link 49 released, the extraction parachute 19 can deploy the main parachute 22.In an emergency, the extraction parachute 19 can be released by energizing a solenoid 90, which causes the rollers 84, 85 to move and release the first link 49. Provided this is done before the platform 10 reaches the fixture 28 on the aircraft floor 16, the extraction parachute 19 is released without deploying the main parachute 22 because the first and second links 49, 50 are not connected to each other.Leger Does Not Disclose One or More Features of Claim 6 Claim 6 recites, in part, an extraction parachute release device configured to uncouple the extraction parachute from the platform;wherein the aerial delivery system comprises an extraction parachute release assembly arranged to cause the extraction parachute release device to uncouple the extraction parachute from the platform in response to the platform moving to a second predetermined position relative to the aircraft; and wherein the second predetermined position is a position reached by the platform after the platform has passed the first predetermined position Leger does not disclose these features.Instead, with respect to the force transfer mechanism of Leger, the locking pin 51 and the rollers 84, 85 are both caused to move when the crank arm 38 passes the fixture 28 on the floor of the aircraft. The force transfer mechanism of Leger thus has a single input means which is activated at a single point during extraction of the platform 10.The force transfer mechanism of Leger is thus configured to, in response to the platform reaching one single predetermined position relative to the aircraft, both: (a) couple the main parachute deployment line 21 to the extraction parachute line 18, and (b) release the extraction parachute.Thus, Leger does not disclose each and every feature of independent claim 6.Further, nothing was cited or found in the other cited art that cures the above-mentioned deficiencies of Leger with respect to independent claim 6. For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claim 6 patentably distinguishes over the cited art.Applicant further submits that the dependent claims inherit the patentable features of base claim 6, and therefore, patentably distinguish over the cited art.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.New Claims New claims 21-29 have been added.New claims 21-27 inherit the patentable features of base claim 6, and therefore, patentably distinguish over the cited art.New claims 28 and 29, both of which have their own scope, have been added to recite one or more features that are similar to independent claim 6.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.CONCLUSIONIn view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that the present application is in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the claims be allowed and the application be passed to issue.Although Applicant has focused the remarks and/or amendments on or primarily on the independent claims in order to expedite the prosecution of the instant application, Applicant reserves the right to remark on and/or amend any of the dependent claims at any time. The mere fact that Applicant has not remarked on and/or amended any of the dependent claims at this time, either related to an Official Notice or not, is unequivocally not an admission of prior art.Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application.Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution.Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.If for any reason the Examiner determines that the application is not now in condition for allowance, it is respectfully requested that the Examiner contact, by telephone, Applicant's undersigned representative at the indicated telephone number to arrange for an interview to expedite the disposition of this application.In the event this paper is not being timely filed, Applicant respectfully petitions for an appropriate extension of time.
